compiled_state.description:
## Problem

On the default (materialized) completion path, a completion-verifier PASS records no material
fingerprint of its own. When it is signed, `verdict_manifest`
(`src/rebar/_commands/completion_bundle.py` ~line 166-170) falls back to
`current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id)`, which reads the LIVE ticket at signing time. A run
takes 9 to 11 minutes. If the description is edited during the run, the signature binds the
EDITED material to a verdict that verified the ORIGINAL text.

A close then reuses it: `_reusable_attested_pass` (`src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py`
~line 154-157) accepts a signed PASS when its signed material equals the ticket's current
fingerprint, which it now does. So the edited text is certified complete without ever being
verified. The close path's own signing (`_sign_completion_and_report`,
`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` ~line 312) checks only code drift
(`verified_at_sha` vs a fresh resolve), not ticket-material drift.

Only the experimental pinned ticket-view mode records the material it read
(`_attach_completion_read_basis`, `src/rebar/llm/completion.py` ~line 157-175). It is off by
default (`verify.completion_pinned_ticket_view = false`) and the committed `rebar.toml` does not
enable it, so the MCP server, CLI, and library all take the unprotected path.

Unlike plan review, there is no under-lock re-check: plan review's `generation.sign_manifest`
re-collects material and raises `PlanReviewGenerationChanged`; completion has no equivalent.

## Evidence (origin/main 82a91a89f1d, in-process, no LLM)

Fresh store, ticket with description D1: fingerprint `1a3ac962405bcd5b`. Edit to D2: fingerprint
`c4d87eb4bcaacafa`. `verdict_manifest` on a default-path PASS (no `completion_read_basis`, no
`material_fingerprint`) emits `material: c4d87eb4bcaacafa` — D2, not D1.

## Root cause confirmed (origin/main f147e08242f, in-process, no LLM)

On the attested materialized path the verifier's ticket tools read a pinned copy of the
tickets branch: `gate_source.attach_materialized_tickets` sets `handle.tickets_path`, and
`runner.py` (~line 394) builds `pai_tools.rebar_tools(cfg.tickets_path or cfg.repo_path, ...)`,
i.e. it treats `tickets_path` as a repo root. Library reads do NOT follow it: inside
`gate_session()` + `use_tickets_root(snapshot)`, `config.tracker_dir()` still returns the live
`.tickets-tracker`. So neither the run nor the signer records the material the verifier read.

Measured: ticket at D1 (fingerprint 5e361259eb5cc4b9), `materialize_tickets()`, edit to D2
(077a5a65ed02ed3f). `current_material_fingerprint(tid, repo_root=snapshot)` returns
5e361259eb5cc4b9 (D1, what the verifier read); the live read, which `verdict_manifest` signs,
returns D2.

## Plan

Plan review already does this correctly: it records the material it reviewed and re-checks it
under the store lock before signing (`generation.sign_manifest`, `under_lock_check`, raising
`PlanReviewGenerationChanged`). Completion will do the same.

1. Capture (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py`): in `_run_completion_at_handle`, when the attested
   handle has a materialized `tickets_path` and no pinned ticket view, set
   `result["material_fingerprint"] = current_material_fingerprint(ticket_id,
   repo_root=handle.tickets_path)` — the snapshot the verifier read. (The pinned-view path already
   records it in `_attach_completion_read_basis`; local source never signs.)
2. Refuse (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py`): `sign_completion_verdict` — the single
   producer seam used by `record_completion_verdict`, the close path
   (`_sign_completion_and_report`), and the op-cert service (`opcert_service/jobs.py`) — signs
   through `signing._sign_manifest_under_lock` with an `under_lock_check` that recomputes the live
   fingerprint and raises `SigningError` when it differs from the recorded read-time material.
   Callers already map `SigningError` to `sign_failed` (no new cause values, so no schema change:
   `transition_result.schema.json` and `common.schema.json` enumerate the causes).
3. Decision: a verifier PASS with NO recorded material (only test fakes and legacy result shapes
   produce one after step 1) keeps today's behaviour. Refusing it would change ~45 test files
   that fake a PASS without material. The residual risk — a future producer that skips step 1 —
   is covered by a test pinning that a real attested run records the read-time material.
   Administrative dispositions (no verifier run) are unchanged: their material is close-time.
4. A refused signature leaves no attestation, so `_reusable_attested_pass` has nothing to reuse
   and a close re-runs verification.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] New `tests/unit/test_completion_signing_material.py`: `_run_completion_at_handle` on an
  attested handle with a materialized snapshot at D1, live store edited to D2, records
  `material_fingerprint == fp(D1)`. Fails on origin/main (no material recorded).
- [x] Same file: `sign_completion_verdict` on a PASS recording fp(D1) after the live ticket moved
  to D2 raises `SigningError` and appends no SIGNATURE event. Fails on origin/main (signs D2).
- [x] Same file: `record_completion_verdict` in that situation returns `signed: False`,
  `cause: "sign_failed"`, and `_reusable_attested_pass` then returns None.
- [x] Same file: unchanged material still signs, and the manifest binds the read-time material.
- [x] Existing completion signing, reuse, and disposition tests pass unchanged.

## Testing
```
.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_completion_signing_material.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_standalone_completion_record.py tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_attestation_reuse.py tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py tests/unit/test_transition_close.py -p no:randomly -q
make lint && make typecheck && make verify
```

sign_completion_verdict re-checks read-time vs live material under the store lock and refuses on mismatch
NEW regression oracle: capture, under-lock refusal, record/reuse outcome, unchanged-material happy path
